messages.author: 9d6f44219e2ec3d4
messages.subject: Calibration of .bin files
parts:
Hi Vincent,

I understand that GGIR will run a auto-calibration algorithm to come up with a calibration error, and the offset is stored in C object of the basic meta RData file. For some of our population level analysis we will need to convert the .bin files into 60s epochs and analyze the data outside of the GGIR package. 

1. How do I use the calibration information to write a new .bin file with the corrected values, and is this necessary? 

2. Also in the newest GENEActiv software, I saw that there is an option for setting z-axis temperature offset when converting to 60s epochs. Does this mean that the software automatically applies the activity based auto-calibration when doing the converting? 

Best,
Mike

messages.author: c4e67f9d1aa89ddc
messages.subject: Re: Calibration of .bin files
parts:
Hi Mike,

As its name indicates it, the autocalibration performed within GGIR is a procedure that measure and correct potential calibration errors.
If calibration error has not been reduced to under 0.01 g., then data are not processed.
Therefore you can use epoch reduced data .csv  as is.
Information regarding autocalibration for processed data may be find is `data_quality_report.csv`

Refer to the original Vincent's paper regarding autocalibration.

Best regards,

Damien

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Calibration of .bin files
parts:
Hi Mike,

The calibration correction is applied within the GGIR analyses and all output GGIR creates is based on the corrected raw data.
If you want to use any software that is not GGIR to convert raw data to 60 second epochs then I cannot guarantee that calibration correction is used. You would have to contact the developers/maintainer of that software. 
I hope this answers your question.

Damien - thanks for your help. Note that if the error is not reduced to under 0.01 the data is still processed but the reported calibration error reduction in the output (e.g. output part2 or object C) should then alarm you as a user to not trust the corresponding results.
Best, Vincent
